Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. content.text:
The problem is clear. `next.config.ts` has `cacheComponents: true`, and `app/product/page.tsx` awaits `getInventory()` at the top level of the page component. Because `getInventory()` calls `connection()`, it's request-time dynamic — so the whole page render, including the static `<h1>`, blocks on that await. There's no static shell to prerender, so nothing paints until the data resolves.

The fix is to move the dynamic read below a Suspense boundary so the title becomes part of the prerendered shell:

content.text:
Only the grep's own shell matched. Done. ## What was wrong `next.config.ts` enables `cacheComponents: true`. In `app/product/page.tsx`, the page component awaited `getInventory()` at its top level, and `getInventory()` calls `connection()` — a request-time API. That await sat above the entire returned tree, so the static `

` was trapped behind it and nothing could be prerendered. The slowness wasn't the real headline, though: **the original code failed `next build` outright.** Next.js diagnosed it precisely: > `connection()` accessed outside of `` prevents the route from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience. > — [stream] Provide a placeholder with `` around the data access So `/product` was a fully blocking route with no static shell at all. ## The fix `app/product/page.tsx` — the page component is now synchronous, holding the static title, with the dynamic read moved into an `` child below a Suspense boundary. `lib/data.ts` is untouched; `connection()` is legitimately request-time and correctly stays uncached. ## Verification Build classification changed from a hard prerender error to: ``` └ ◐ /product (Partial Prerender) prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content ``` The prerendered `.next/server/app/product.html` contains `

Premium Widget

` and the fallback, and contains **zero** occurrences of the inventory data — confirming the title is genuinely in the static shell rather than merely arriving fast. To measure the split I temporarily added a 3s delay to `getInventory()` and streamed the response from a production server: ``` title/fallback : 0.073s inventory data : 3.073s ``` The title paints at 73ms while data resolves 3s later. I then removed that delay and re-verified the final build — `lib/data.ts` is back to its committed content. One note: `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` on its own (`jsx: preserve` → `react-jsx`, added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts`, reformatted arrays). That's Next.js's automatic reconfiguration, not something I chose; it'll recur on any build. Revert it if you'd rather keep it out of your diff. The pre-existing `package.json` modification was there before I started. Since navigation is client-side via ``, you'll now get the title instantly on click with the inventory streaming in — worth a quick look in the browser to confirm the fallback reads well at real-world latency, since `Loading inventory…` is a placeholder you may want styled to match the final layout and avoid a shift.
